question.text: `Saksham Skills Pvt Ltd` is incorporated as a Section 8 company under the Companies Act 2013. Which of the following statements about Section 8 companies is CORRECT?

answer.text: A Section 8 company can distribute dividends up to 10% of profit to its members
A Section 8 company must apply its profits (or other income) toward promoting its objects and is PROHIBITED from paying any dividend to its members
A Section 8 company is not required to hold any licence from the Registrar of Companies (ROC)
A Section 8 company automatically qualifies as a SE under SEBI ICDR, without any further eligibility test

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 8(1) requires a Section 8 company to apply its profits, if any, or other income in promoting its objects and PROHIBITS payment of any dividend to its members. A licence from the ROC (Central Government delegate) is mandatory. It does NOT automatically qualify as SE — it still must pass the 16-activity / 67% test under ICDR Reg 292B. The Trap: Dividend distribution (any %) violates Section 8. Option C is wrong — ROC licence is mandatory. Option D conflates Companies-Act Section 8 form with SEBI SE eligibility — these are two separate tests. Cross-Exam Context: X-A / X-B (Investment Adviser) may advise HNIs on forming Section 8 for family philanthropy; XXIII tests the SE-eligibility interplay. Section 8 form is necessary-but-not-sufficient for SSE listing. Assessor's Pro-Tip: During fieldwork, ask for the Section 8 licence number and cross-check MCA portal. Then independently verify the 67% eligibility under Reg 292B — the SE Board cannot rely on 'we are Section 8' to bypass the ICDR test.
